questions.stem: A client asks a safety professional to certify a complex structural design outside the professional’s education and experience. What is the ethical response?
options: Decline or limit the assignment and involve a qualified professional while clearly communicating the boundaries of competence
Certify it because a general safety credential covers every engineering specialty
Approve it if the client accepts responsibility in writing
Copy a prior design and omit the limitation from the report
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Professionals should undertake work only within their competence and seek qualified assistance when needed. Client pressure or waiver does not create expertise.
incorrectOptionExplanations: The option 'Certify it because a general safety credential covers every engineering specialty' does not apply the controlling principle for professional competence to the facts given, so it is not the best answer.
The option 'Approve it if the client accepts responsibility in writing' does not apply the controlling principle for professional competence to the facts given, so it is not the best answer.
The option 'Copy a prior design and omit the limitation from the report' does not apply the controlling principle for professional competence to the facts given, so it is not the best answer.

Keep the interest secret because the vendor’s work may be competent
Increase the consulting fee so the financial relationship becomes immaterial
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Actual or apparent conflicts should be disclosed and managed so professional judgment and client trust are not compromised.
incorrectOptionExplanations: The option 'Recommend the vendor as the only option without comparing alternatives' does not apply the controlling principle for conflict of interest to the facts given, so it is not the best answer.
The option 'Keep the interest secret because the vendor’s work may be competent' does not apply the controlling principle for conflict of interest to the facts given, so it is not the best answer.

The option 'Increase the consulting fee so the financial relationship becomes immaterial' does not apply the controlling principle for conflict of interest to the facts given, so it is not the best answer.

Alter only the electronic version and retain the original privately
Refuse to falsify the record, preserve accurate information, and escalate the integrity concern through appropriate channels
Change the date because the concentration result did not change

Withhold all results until uncertainty can be eliminated

The option 'Withhold all results until uncertainty can be eliminated' does not apply the controlling principle for objective communication of uncertainty to the facts given, so it is not the best answer.

questions.stem: At a competence boundary review, a supervisor proposes: "Change the date because the concentration result did not change". The underlying case is: Management asks a CSP to change a sampling date so an overdue test appears timely. The result itself is accurate. What should the CSP do? Which alternative is the most defensible correction?
options: Refuse to falsify the record, preserve accurate information, and escalate the integrity concern through appropriate channels
Delete the record and collect a new sample without documenting the gap
Change the date because the concentration result did not change
Alter only the electronic version and retain the original privately
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Professional records must be truthful and complete. Falsifying timing misrepresents compliance and undermines evidence integrity even when the numerical result is valid.
incorrectOptionExplanations: The proposed response 'Delete the record and collect a new sample without documenting the gap' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling truthful professional records principle.
The proposed response 'Change the date because the concentration result did not change' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling truthful professional records principle.
The proposed response 'Alter only the electronic version and retain the original privately' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling truthful professional records principle.
